question: Will U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs record a single-day net inflow exceeding $500 million on any trading day between August 31 and September 7, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves YES if, on any U.S. equity trading day from August 31, 2026 through September 4, 2026 (inclusive), the aggregate net flow across all U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs is greater than +$500 million (i.e. a value above 500.0 in the "Total" row, expressed in US$m), as reported in the Bitcoin ETF Flow table at https://farside.co.uk/btc/ . For example, a "Total" of 606.3 for a given date resolves YES; a "Total" of 307.5 does not. Otherwise it resolves NO. (September 7, 2026 is Labor Day, when U.S. equity markets and these ETFs do not trade, so no flows occur on that date.)
reference_class: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF trading days in 2026 (and the Aug-2026 sub-class) with aggregate Farside net flow above +$500m

Three of five eligible sessions (Aug 31, Sep 1, Sep 2) are published Farside Totals of +216.7, -236.5, +101.1 — all far short — so YES requires Sep 3 (closed, unpublished at Now) or Sep 4 alone to clear +500. Base rate: ~3-4% of 2026 sessions cleared +500; even August 2026, the year's best month (+$3.52bn, 16/21 positive, a nine-session streak), produced exactly 2 of 21 (~9.5%), both mid-streak and consecutive. That streak regime has ended: Aug 28 was an outflow, Sep 1 was the largest single-day outflow since Jul 31, and the trailing five sessions average roughly zero with ~200 SD, so +500 is a ~2.5-sigma print. Conditioning up: Sep 3 was a genuine rally session — BTC ran from ~$77.8k to ~$81.3k on Waller's rate-pause signal, Strategy resumed buying, ETH/XRP ETF demand is live — and creation surges cluster on exactly this setup (Aug 19/20). Capping that: price-to-flow transmission has been weak all week (Sep 2 was an up day for only +101m), the closest in-regime analogue (Aug 25's squeeze to ~$81.1k) delivered just +314 with +232 follow-through, and a 500 total essentially requires IBIT alone near +400 versus a recent best of ~+278. I price Sep 3 at ~10% and Sep 4 — pre-Labor-Day Friday, two-sided NFP, plus some chance its row is not published by the 2026-09-05T00:00Z stamp — at ~5%, positively correlated, giving ~12%.
what_would_change_my_mind: Farside's Sep 3 total posting above ~+400m, showing the flow response to this week's rally is much larger than Sep 1-2 implied
BTC extending sharply higher on Sep 4 (e.g. a decisive break above ~$85k) with intraday IBIT creation reports in the hundreds of millions
Evidence of a single large allocator/seed creation queued into IBIT or a new fund launch landing in the window
Confirmation that Sep 4's Farside figure will not publish before the resolution timestamp, which would leave Sep 3 as the only remaining chance

question: What will Bitcoin's price be on September 4, 2026?
resolution_criterion: This question resolves to the closing price of Bitcoin (BTC) in US dollars for September 4, 2026 (UTC), as reported in the "Close" column of the CoinGecko Bitcoin historical data page: https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin/historical_data. For example, a close of $77,378 resolves as 77378. If CoinGecko does not publish a close value for September 4, 2026, the closing price reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) for that date (UTC) will be used instead.
reference_class: One-day-ahead changes in BTC's UTC daily close during the current high-volatility regime (trailing 30 daily closes, CoinGecko, 2026-08-04 to 2026-09-03)
dispersion_basis: SD of daily UTC-close log returns over trailing 30 days from CoinGecko market_chart = 2.38%, x 2.56 = 6.09% of spot ($81,224) = $4,946, scaled by sqrt(25.3h/24h) = $5,070

supervisor.reconciliation: FACTUAL 1 - does a Polymarket Sep-4 BTC book exist? Run 2 reported a liquid ladder (~$516k liquidity, ~$1.27M volume, dense strikes $76-88k, noon-ET settlement off Binance BTC/USDT); Runs 1 and 3 reported retrieval failures, with Run 3 saying the Gamma API returned nothing. The harness's own candidate list corroborates Run 2: multiple Sep-4/5/6/7 BTC strike contracts with real volume (31,993 on the <$70,000 Sep 4 book). Absence of retrieval is not absence of a market, so I side with Run 2 on existence. The harness prices are only weakly informative on level - <$70,000 at 0.00 and $70-72k at 0.00 merely confirm that a >13% one-day drop is priced near zero, consistent with spot at $81.2k and with all three runs. Run 2's specific implied sigma (2.0% to 16:00Z) and fat-tail read (P(>84k)=6.9%) I could not verify on this run with no web access, so I treat it as directional support for a ~2.4% baseline rather than as a hard anchor. Its noted contract mismatch (8 hours short of our snapshot, single-venue USDT pair vs CoinGecko USD aggregate) is real and correctly handled by sqrt-time scaling. FACTUAL 2 - was spot sampled at an intraday high? Run 1 argued yes and tilted the median down for spike-fade; Run 3's finer data shows the high was $81,731 at ~20:00Z and price had already eased to ~$81,186 by 22:49Z. Run 3 is right: roughly 0.7% of the fade has already occurred, which removes most of Run 1's justification for centering below spot. I therefore center essentially at spot and express the give-back risk as mild left skew instead of a shifted median. FACTUAL 3 - NFP inside the window: all three agree the August Employment Situation prints 2026-09-04 12:30Z, inside the window. Settled, and it argues for width, not direction. FACTUAL 4 - instrument precision: Run 3 flagged a ~1% reconciliation gap between the question background's Aug 21 close ($77,378) and CoinGecko's own 00:00Z snapshots. Real but small and unresolvable here; it is a further argument against a narrow band

Resolution is the CoinGecko UTC close for Sep 4, i.e. the price at 2026-09-05T00:00Z, ~25.3h from Now; the resolution day has not begun. At a one-day horizon BTC is a near-martingale, so the center is current spot (~$81,190-81,230 at 22:42-22:49Z Sep 3) rather than a trend extrapolation of the +5.4% session. Directional evidence is genuinely two-sided: real repricing catalysts (Waller signalling a September hold, US-Iran de-escalation, DXY below 99, ~$2.8B ETF inflows, Strategy resuming purchases) against squeeze mechanics (~$164M shorts liquidated vs ~$7.3M longs), overbought readings, twelve prior sessions that failed to hold above $80k, and standing macro headwinds (WTI >$90, 10y near 4.81%). I take spot with only a token tilt: the intraday high of $81,731 (20:00Z) has already faded ~0.7%, so the spike-fade argument is partly spent, but I keep a mild left skew for squeeze give-back. Width is the substantive call: the trailing-30d SD (2.38%) and the market-implied ~2.4% agree, and I widen to ~2.8% for vol clustering after a 5.4% day plus the August NFP print at 12:30Z inside the window. Both bounds require a one-day move of -32% or +23%, never observed outside March-2020-class events, so no escape mass is declared.
what_would_change_my_mind: A sharp reversal in the remaining ~1.25h of Sept 3 UTC that resets the starting level for the window
An NFP print far outside the 102k/-25k consensus range, or an unusually hawkish/dovish Fed reaction to it
Reversal of the US/Iran de-escalation headline that triggered today's 5% move
A large single-day ETF outflow print or a resumption of the late-August liquidation pattern
